abstract: Somatic aberrations have been extensively characterized in multiple myeloma (MM). However, the mutational processes underlying small insertions and deletions (InDels) remain poorly understood. Here, we used a recently developed 89-channel InDel classification schema which allows differentiating mutational processes. We analyzed whole-genome sequencing data from 887 MM samples, spanning both newly diagnosed (NDMM) and relapsed/refractory disease (RRMM). We identified InDel signatures associated with replication slippage, APOBEC mutagenesis, topoisomerase 1 (TOP1)-mediated mutagenesis, non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), and two rare DNA damage repair-deficiency signatures. In two randomized clinical trials, incorporation of the APOBEC InDel signature InD9a improved treatment outcome prediction as pertaining to progression-free survival (PFS) and achievement of minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity. InD29, a signature linked to NHEJ-mediated errors, was detected in both NDMM and RRMM, and was enriched in samples exhibiting melphalan-associated mutagenesis and high SV burden. Genome-wide analysis identified a recurrent InDel hotspot at TXNDC5, a highly expressed gene in MM located within a region implicated in complex genomic rearrangements, with predominantly noncoding alterations suggesting potential regulatory consequences. Finally, InDel signatures revealed the presence of mismatch-repair deficiency (MMRd) and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) phenotypes, even in cases without germline predisposition. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive characterization of InDel mutagenesis in MM, revealing previously underexplored relationships and demonstrating potential to refine comprehensive genomic classifications of MM.
